flags.title: No Venetian structure sheet states a single-entry or freezeout rule
flags.detail: All 37 official structure sheets were read on 2026-11-17. Not one contains the words 'single entry', 'one entry', 'freezeout' or 'no re-entry'. Every one-day sheet is simply silent on re-entry, rebuy and add-on. Silence is not a prohibition, so no event is marked 'single-entry confirmed'.
flags.impact: The confirmed-only toggle returns zero rows. Rules-silent candidates have a separate group filter and remain unconfirmed.

flags.title: Two events price a second buy-in on the official sheet
flags.detail: Events 18 and 58 ($200 Valuetown Bounty) print: 'PokerAtlas PRO players will receive a twenty ($20) rake discount on their initial $200 buy in only ... All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200.' Pricing a subsequent buy-in means more than one buy-in per player is contemplated.
flags.impact: Events 18 and 58 are moved out of the single-entry candidate group.

flags.title: The official schedule PDF has a garbled date column on 12 rows
flags.detail: In dse-nov-2026-schedule.pdf the DATE cell on 12 rows prints a sponsor banner ('@PokerAtlas PRO', '@PokerAtlas* TOUR') or a series logo ('LIPS CHAMPIONSHIP ...') instead of the date. Those rows are events 17, 18, 32, 33, 35, 36, 39, 40, 46, 47 (1A), 49 (1A and 1B) and 58.
flags.impact: Every affected date was recovered from the official HTML schedule page and is marked 'date from HTML' in the row detail. The PDF alone is not sufficient to place those events.

flags.title: Bounty guarantees include bounty money, so they are not like-for-like
flags.detail: Bounty and PKO sheets state the guarantee 'consists of the actual prize pool plus the total amount of bounties that are awarded'. A $8,000 bounty guarantee is therefore a smaller cash prize pool than a $8,000 non-bounty guarantee.
flags.impact: Bounty events are shown in a separate group and are never mixed into the like-for-like ranking.

flags.title: No official finish time is published for any event
flags.detail: The schedule gives start time, registration close, chips and level length, but no end time. A finish time cannot be derived without a field size, which the organiser does not publish in advance.
flags.impact: The day plan compares start order with the later registration deadline. A later event is conditional, not a guaranteed sequence; no unconfirmed event becomes a primary.

flags.title: No like-for-like checkout totals were confirmed
flags.detail: A Venetian Dec 1–4 lookup for one adult loaded an official booking shell without a price. Wynn showed partial Nov 18–19 rates for a different stay, which cannot be compared. Neither supplied a verified itemized total or rate timestamp for the research stay.
flags.impact: Do not rank hotels by the partial rates or assume availability. See the exact-stay hotel log.

flags.title: Cancellation deadlines are partial: two properties publish 72 hours, the rest do not
flags.detail: Partly resolved on 2026-11-17 by reading each property's own terms page first-hand. Bellagio and MGM Grand both publish a 72-hour window: the first night's deposit is fully refundable if Room Reservations is told at least 72 hours before arrival, and a late cancellation or no-show forfeits it. Caesars Palace and Horseshoe advertise 'FREE 48-Hour Cancellation*' with an asterisk whose condition is not printed on the page read. The Venetian and Palazzo publish no poker-rate deadline, but do publish that prepaid offers are non-cancellable and non-refundable unless the offer says otherwise, and that checking out early costs $100 plus tax. Wynn publishes deposit terms only (one night charged at booking) and no refund window.
flags.impact: For a Bellagio or MGM Grand stay you can plan a refundable hold until 72 hours out. For the Venetian poker rate, which is the rate this plan depends on, the deadline is still not established, so treat the deposit as committed.

flags.title: Room tax: the hotel's own terms are re-read, the county levy is not
flags.detail: 13.38% comes from Clark County's own 'General Information Guide for Transient Lodging Establishments' and is corroborated by the Venetian's hotel terms. It was read on 2026-11-16 by an earlier session and was not re-read today.

flags.detail: The properties charge more than the nightly rate and resort fee in two ways a rate comparison misses. The Venetian and Palazzo add $50 per night for each additional guest 13 or older above double occupancy, and $100 plus tax for checking out before the scheduled departure date. Bellagio adds $50 plus tax per occupant per night above two. MGM Grand adds $40 plus tax per occupant per night above two. Caesars Palace and Horseshoe do not publish an occupancy charge on the page read.
flags.impact: As a pair, the published rates and the calculator are right. With a third adult in the room the nightly cost rises by $50 (Venetian) or $40 (MGM Grand) plus tax, which can exceed the difference between two hotels.

questions.q: What entry rule qualifies an event?
questions.why: Only a written whole-event cap of one entry, with no paid rebuy or add-on, satisfies this trip's policy.
questions.blocks: A bookable poker itinerary until an organizer supplies those written terms.

questions.q: Which dates should be tested before booking?
questions.why: Hotel rates, walking plans and the day-by-day schedule are all date-bound. The poker suite rate is only quoted 150 days out and only by phone.

questions.q: Which budget and quality screen should the first hotel pass use?
questions.why: Compare like-for-like checkout totals after checking the room amenities and walking eligibility.
questions.blocks: The hotel shortlist and ranking until checkout and room features are verified.
questions.answer: Research screen, not a preference claim: $200/night all-in, private nonsmoking room with ensuite bath, and a refundable booking with a published deadline.

questions.q: Can a primary and conditional fallback fit without assuming an early exit?
questions.why: You asked to play from 8 AM onward. The earliest verified Venetian start in this series is 9:10 AM (satellite event 46) and 10:10 AM for a main-schedule event.
questions.answer: One qualified primary per day; switch only if it is skipped or the player is free in time. No qualified primary or fallback verified.

questions.why: Events 24, 32 and 49 are Seniors events with a hard 50+ rule and no refund for an under-50 entrant. They carry $40K, $40K and $300K guarantees, three of the larger figures in the series.

questions.q: Do you have, or will you open, a Venetian Rewards card?
questions.why: Every structure sheet requires one to participate, and the poker suite rate is tracked through it.
questions.blocks: Both entering any Venetian event and qualifying for any quoted poker suite rate.

questions.q: Do you object to bounty formats on principle, or only to paying extra for an advantage?
questions.why: A bounty does not establish whether extra spending is allowed. Its guarantee can include bounty money and is not like-for-like with a cash-only guarantee.
questions.blocks: Whether the 30 bounty and PKO events belong in your plan.

questions.q: Is a paid PokerAtlas PRO membership acceptable?
questions.why: It buys a $20 rake discount on Valuetown events 18 and 58 and on the first buy-in only. That is a spend-to-advantage element.
Parking adds $20-$40 a day at the Venetian unless you qualify for free self-parking through play or tier status. It changes the true nightly cost.
questions.blocks: The parking line in the true-cost calculator.

questions.q: Do you want the Day 2 restarts counted as playable days?
questions.why: Twelve rows in the schedule are Day 2 / Day 3 / final-table restarts. They cost nothing extra but occupy a morning or afternoon.
questions.blocks: The day plan for 12 of the 38 series days.

questions.q: Should satellites be in the plan?
questions.why: Events 33, 37, 41, 44, 45, 46 and 48 award seats, not cash. They are cheap ways into Event 39 or 47 but they are not prize-money events.

questions.q: How much variance do you accept on the guarantee-to-buy-in ratio?
questions.why: The ratio is descriptive, not a forecast. A $500K guarantee on an $800 buy-in is a floor set by the room; the actual pool depends on entries.
questions.blocks: How the ranking column should be read.

questions.q: Will you travel with more than two adults in the room?
questions.why: The Venetian, Palazzo, Bellagio and MGM Grand all surcharge a third adult, from $40 to $50 plus tax per night, which changes the cheapest-hotel answer.
questions.blocks: The hotel half of the trip cost and the cost comparison between properties.

questions.q: Do you accept a booking with no published cancellation deadline?
questions.why: The Venetian poker rate, which the whole plan leans on, publishes no cancellation deadline. Bellagio and MGM Grand publish 72 hours. Booking the Venetian means treating the deposit as committed.
